obituary.name: Eleanor B. Screenphone
obituary.headline: Screenphone, 5, offered many connections

cause.text: She quietly went dark after the spiderweb cracks appeared across her display.

life.text: For years, she served as a repository for fleeting moments, bearing multiple surface scratches from the kitchen counter.
The deep accumulation of general surface grime marked her long hours beside the sofa.
Her final presentation was marked by the distinctive red bottom bezel, a signature of her later years.

obituary.survived_by: a charging cable coiled near the mantelpiece and the slightly sticky remote control.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please wipe down the tablet screen with a dry cloth.
obituary.epitaph: A million small signals, finally quiet.

obituary.name: Mildred W. Wirecoil
obituary.headline: Mildred, a long run, now at rest

cause.text: She met her end after a significant tearing of her outer sheath.

life.text: Mildred spent many years running across the floorboards, her white outer casing providing dependable passage.
A valued member of the setup, her white exterior allowed her to travel from the skirting to the armchair.
Her inner workings were once so neatly contained, a quiet service provided to the radio stand.

obituary.survived_by: the spare extension cord and a dust bunny of particular girth.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: we ask that the nearest plug be checked for warmth.
obituary.epitaph: Always connected, even when the weave gives way.

drafts.name: Alastair White Wiresworth
drafts.headline: Wiresworth, a connector, gave his all.

cause_of_death.text: Alastair passed away when a section of his casing tore open, exposing his inner workings.

life.text: His years were marked by dutiful transport throughout the study, where the dirt settled upon his white outer casing (d3, d4).
He provided reliable extension for the reading lamp near the skirting board, his reach extending out toward the bookshelf (d5).
His consistent service meant he saw many quiet evenings spent near the mahogany sideboard.

drafts.survived_by: the power outlet it could not reach and a length of unused cordage.
drafts.in_lieu_of_flowers: In lieu of flowers, please ensure the main socket is free of any dust accumulation.
drafts.epitaph: The signal reached its final destination.

obituary.name: Augustus 'Augie' Canvasfoot
obituary.headline: A reliable tread that wore thin

cause.text: His service concluded following the split sole on the upper shoe.

life.text: Augie was a lifelong member of the outdoor excursions, his light brown canvas material enduring countless walks across the gravel drive.
He was particularly noted for the fraying around his edges while navigating muddy patches near the vegetable patch.
The lower shoe, after years of service, finally developed a noticeable tear in its fabric, marking the end of his sturdy career.

obituary.survived_by: a well-used boot with a similar hue and a collection of unmatched trowels.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please ensure the dustpan is kept level.
obituary.epitaph: Many paths were trod, quietly and well.

obituary.name: Algernon Brownsworth, S. Toast
obituary.headline: A fine, square offering to the morning hour

cause.text: His final moments arrived following a significant browning of his surface.

life.text: Algernon was a perfectly square fixture, a product of careful slicing. He provided a respectable golden brown crust during breakfast by the small oak table.
Though his edges began to darken, he maintained a good discoloration throughout his service, often being the first item sought by the household staff.

obituary.survived_by: a rather dense jar of marmalade and a slightly chipped ceramic butter dish.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: we request that the crumb tray be emptied forthwith.
obituary.epitaph: The warmth was fleeting, but the effort was sound.

obituary.name: Mrs. Clara Creamsworth
obituary.headline: Creamer, 4, offered richness to many mornings

cause.text: Her service concluded following a fissure that appeared on her side.

life.text: Mrs. Creamsworth was a valued vessel, offering her contents via her pouring spout throughout many breakfast gatherings.
Throughout her time in the pantry, she bore the marks of service, including a faint brown marking and the trace of a yellow line within her side.

obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please ensure the crumb tray is thoroughly emptied.

obituary.name: Clarissa Glazenbrook
obituary.headline: A fine vessel, now scattered to the floor

cause.text: Clarissa passed away when several pieces of her clear glass shattered.

life.text: She spent many years proudly displaying small, hardy foliage, her faceted base catching the light near the sideboard.
Her rim, once perfectly formed, showed the subtle marks of years of careful placement upon the mantle.
The loss of certain segments, now gone, leaves a gap in the collection on the mantelpiece.

obituary.survived_by: a rather dull salt shaker and the brass letter opener.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: we ask that the dustpan be given a thorough cleaning.
obituary.epitaph: Held moments, now yielding to the quiet earth.

obituary.name: Mr. Josiah Gourdington
obituary.headline: A Kindly Light, Now Dimmed

cause.text: His final decline was marked by the spreading rot.

life.text: He spent his autumn showing his cheerful orange color and carved jack-o'-lantern faces, much loved on the porch stoop.
He gathered a fine layer of dirt while presiding over the autumn harvest display near the back step.
The small stem, his distinctive hallmark, was always present during the evening's illumination.

obituary.survived_by: a patch of moss and one very small, slightly dusty napkin ring.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please wipe down the kitchen counter thoroughly.
obituary.epitaph: His light shone brightly, though the season turned.

cause.text: He passed away after a final, intense surge resulted in a charred surface.

life.text: He provided steady illumination in the hall, his earthen tone glass showing pleasing discoloration on glass.

obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please wipe down the adjacent skirting board.

obituary.name: Prudence Terracotta-Flesh
obituary.headline: Rosette Form, Faded Gently

cause.text: Prudence passed away following the development of darkened and discolored leaves.

life.text: For many seasons, she presented her fleshy, rosette shape upon the sill, often gathering fine soil and gravel residue.
Her pale green and brown leaves provided quiet structure to the collection, resting comfortably in her terracotta pot.
She maintained her low profile throughout the summers, a steady presence on the mantelpiece.

obituary.survived_by: a very absorbent coaster and a small, ornamental thimble.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please ensure the windowsill is wiped down thoroughly.
obituary.epitaph: Sustaining grace, even when slightly browned.

obituary.name: Mr. Augustus Circuitry
obituary.headline: Adapter, a fixture of the electric circuit

cause.text: He came to an end following the loss of a mounting screw.

life.text: His black plastic casing bore numerous scuffs, having seen regular use near the writing desk.
The white printed text on his exterior served faithfully while he sat near the old oak shelf.
He possessed circular cutouts which accommodated the varied demands of the drawing-room appliances.

obituary.survived_by: a tangle of charging cables and one particularly heavy rubber foot.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please wipe down the nearest appliance housing.
obituary.epitaph: The power flows, though the connection is undone.

obituary.name: Mrs. Veronica Scarlet Canopy
obituary.headline: A splash of bold colour, after many seasons

cause.text: Her structure gave way, finally ripped by the elements.

life.text: She provided much cheer, her bright red hue adorning the entryway during several unexpected showers.
For years, she held her form neatly folded in the hall closet, ready for the next deluge.

obituary.survived_by: a slightly damp dustpan and one overly polished shoe.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please ensure the small brass hook is wiped down weekly.
obituary.epitaph: Held the rain off. Now, only stillness.

obituary.name: Mr. Silas Roast-Bean
obituary.headline: A deep, dark offering to the mornings

cause.text: Natural causes. It was simply no longer needed.

life.text: Mr. Roast-Bean spent many years dispensing his dark brown beans, a quiet ritual often observed by the kitchen table.
His final acts involved a gentle scattering upon the wood floor near the hearth, leaving a subtle, rich aroma.

obituary.survived_by: a measuring spoon perpetually half-full and a bag of sugar from the pantry.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please ensure the grinder blades are wiped free of fine residue.
obituary.epitaph: A fine aroma to begin the day anew.

obituary.name: Agnes Petalworth, Bloom
obituary.headline: A quiet light in the morning light

cause.text: Agnes passed away after a translucent upper bloom appeared.

life.text: Her smooth, cylindrical stem bore a gentle green discoloration while residing near the kitchen sill.
She offered a soft, glowing appearance throughout the afternoons, often situated on the hall stand.
The bright yellow-green top provided a measure of necessary cheer to the little study.

obituary.survived_by: a watering can with a perpetually sticky spout and a collection of overlooked coasters.
obituary.in_lieu_of_flowers: please ensure the dustpan is kept nearby and ready.
obituary.epitaph: It simply wanted to be seen, even when it dimmed.
